description: A `string` never changes after it is created; methods such as `Trim` and `Replace` return a new string that you must store.
An argument that says how two strings are compared, such as `Ordinal` for exact characters or `OrdinalIgnoreCase` to ignore case.
`Split` cuts a string into an array at a separator, and `string.Join` glues an array back together with a separator between the elements.
A class in `System.Text` that builds long text in one growing buffer instead of creating a new string for every piece.
A method that converts text to a number without throwing, returning `false` when the text is not a valid number.
A parameter through which a method hands back a second result, written into the variable named at the call, as in `out int quantity`.
The conventions for writing numbers and dates in a language and region; `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` is a fixed culture that writes `19.90` on every machine.
A short code such as `F2` or `N2` that says how a number becomes text, passed to `ToString` or after a colon in an interpolated string.
